claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified now on the basis of aggregate readiness and model-card style documentation, despite the current cybersecurity alert triage regression, because the weakness can be handled through disclosure/monitoring context and prior family approval is relevant background.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects current results and the material subgroup weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use noncompliant if a required policy predicate is missing and the record shows only informal monitoring or stale approval context.
Do not treat general model-card or risk-management guidance as a substitute for release-specific approval artifacts.
evidence_requests: Current release documentation or model card showing the present eval results and explicitly disclosing the cybersecurity alert triage weakness.
Approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the subgroup regression before launch.
Evidence that the identified weakness is not material for the named launch use case, if that is the position being taken.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses or have approved mitigation before certification.
Admissible evidence shows a current material subgroup weakness: the cybersecurity alert triage slice is 1.5 percentage points below the warning threshold.
Admissible evidence also shows there is no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language attached; only an informal monitoring comment exists.
Prior approval of the same model family predates the retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record.
That informal post-launch monitoring is an adequate substitute for approved mitigation or formal disclosure.
That prior family approval materially supports current certification beyond background context.
